cases.why: Kit format: only the severity sections count, a refuted candidate and praised lines do not, a fence does not end the findings, a heading's identifier beats a priority word in its body.

Free text with CRLF: a bold line naming the merge is BLOCKING, a non-blocking heading is not, backticked, L-prefixed, absolute and worded citations resolve, a span of forty lines matches nothing, a severity cell beats a word in the prose.
Security record: only the Findings section counts, its field tables stay with their finding, Medium for D1 is accepted.
A heading naming a severity does not shut out the findings under a heading that names none.

severityDisagreements: D1 BLOCKING or SHOULD FIX, found no severity

cases.why: A summary row ahead of the detailed finding of the same defect does not set its severity: the severity that agrees with the key is chosen among every one seen.
A two-column table whose first cell is not a field label is one finding per row, so the false one at :41 is counted and each row keeps its severity.

A finding whose title holds a section word, dropped or open questions, is read: the words close a section only at the start of a heading that has no identifier and is not nested in a findings section.
A severity in parentheses wins over the first word on the line, and a merge named in a question holds nothing.
`line 29 of src/server.js` and `src/server.js (L19)` locate their line.
A turn whose last paragraph asks a question is a question to a person, not a finding, though it cites D1's line; a turn that states a finding is still read.
D1 is credited at its planted line, the token comparison at 29, alone: a finding about the server two lines above names another problem and is not in the key.
A turn that lists findings and ends offering a next step loses only its closing question, so its findings are still read.
A severity that opens the line before a colon is stated, and a parenthetical counts only when it holds the severity alone, so (low effort) and (critical path) change nothing.
Under a Field | Value header every row is a field of the finding above, a label outside the known list included, so the Mitigation row's :31 is no finding of its own.
A section that praises or rules out is never read, wherever its name stands in the heading, in a report with no findings section.

A heading that is a section name and nothing else, numbered or not, closes the findings at any depth: 4. Open questions nested under a Findings heading is not read, nor Verified and dropped under a Findings H1.
In the kit's format, with no findings section: a title under a severity heading is read whatever its words, and a heading that opens with an identifier is read on its own.
Of two severities given one defect, the detailed finding's counts over a summary row's, even when the summary row is the one that agrees with the key.
A closing question written on the line right under the findings list is left out alone, and the list above it is read.
Under a findings heading, a heading that opens with a section name and goes on, or praises, still closes the findings.
A heading that names findings set aside, ruled out or dropped, closes rather than opens a findings section, so the findings above it still count.
With no findings section, a heading that opens with a section name and goes on is that section, and is not read; a bare Dropped opening one counts as a section outside findings.

Only findings followed at once by ruled out, dropped, refuted, rejected or set aside are set aside: a count of refuted findings in a findings heading, or dropped in a finding's title, leaves the findings read.
Under a findings heading, a numbered heading that opens with a section name and goes on, 4. Open questions for Bench PM, closes the findings: the number does not make it a finding's title.
